## Solutions — things Azad gets hired for (source: /solutions)

### AI Workflow Automation

Hook: When repetitive work starts stealing real work.

Problem: Teams glue their tools together by hand: answering the same WhatsApp questions, retyping emails into the CRM, juggling calendars, chasing payments and compiling the same report every Friday.

Capabilities:
- AI agents on phone, WhatsApp, email and chat that answer, book and follow up
- Calendars, maps, payments and sign-in connected into one flow
- CRM, ERP, accounts and spreadsheets kept in sync, data entered once
- Reports, alerts and approvals that arrive by themselves

Typical customers: Startups, Sales teams, Operations, Service businesses

How it's used:
- Distribution & wholesale: A won deal becomes an order, an invoice and a stock reservation without anyone retyping it.
- Finance & accounts: Overdue invoices are chased on schedule, with the right reminder for each customer.
- Operations: Low stock raises a draft purchase order for someone to approve.
- Sales: New enquiries are logged and followed up on time, so none go cold.

Why it's different:
- Built around your real process: the exceptions, approvals and hand-offs, not just the tidy path.
- Every automated step leaves a trail of who, what and when, so you can check it or undo it.
- People stay in charge: anything unusual goes to a person instead of being pushed through.

In Azad's words: Most automation projects don't fail because of the model. They fail because nobody mapped the boring parts: which inbox, which field, who approves, what happens when the data is wrong. I start there. I sit with the person doing the work, write down every step, and only then decide where an LLM actually earns its place. Everything else stays deterministic, logged and easy to undo. You get a workflow your team trusts enough to stop double-checking.

Example walkthrough (illustrative sample, not a client case): input "Hi — we're a 40-person logistics company looking at your fleet dashboard. Could someone send pricing for 25 seats and book a call next week? — Priya, Ops Lead, Northwind Freight" → Classify: Intent: sales enquiry · Priority: high · Language: English; Extract: Contact: Priya (Ops Lead) · Company: Northwind Freight · Seats: 25; Enrich: Company size 40 → segment: SMB · Existing CRM record: none; Act: Create lead + deal in CRM (sandbox) · Stage: Qualified; Draft: Reply with pricing tier + 3 call slots, queued for rep approval → Result: Lead created, deal opened, reply drafted, #sales notified — 0 fields typed by a human.

### Computer Vision & Robotics

Hook: When a machine has to see, know where things are, and act on it.

Problem: Robots and vehicles need perception that holds up in the field: on small edge hardware, in changing light, with sensors that drift out of alignment. Models that shine on a benchmark often stall on a real camera stream.

Capabilities:
- Computer vision: object detection, instance segmentation, pose and keypoints, multi-object tracking
- Geometric vision: camera–LiDAR calibration, multi-camera fusion, bird's-eye views, monocular depth
- 3D perception: LiDAR point clouds, ground-plane projection, where every object is in the world
- Robotics: perception that drives decisions on autonomous mobile robots, plus mapping and navigation
- Edge deployment: real time on industrial edge computers and AI accelerators, with the speed–accuracy trade-off measured
- Field validation: tracked experiments and repeatable tests, so every model change is measured before it ships

Typical customers: Robotics & AMRs, Automotive & ADAS, Physical AI, Warehousing, Manufacturing

How it's used:
- Robotics & AMRs: Detect, track and estimate the pose of people, pallets and trolleys so robots move safely and pick the right thing.
- Automotive & ADAS: Surround view and blind-spot warnings from the cameras already on the vehicle, running on its own computer.
- Physical AI & humanoids: Turn cameras and LiDAR into a 3D picture of the world a robot can act on: what is there, where, and how it's moving.
- Warehousing & logistics: Track carts, forklifts and people across the floor in real time, on hardware that fits on the machine.
- Manufacturing & inspection: Spot defects, missing parts and misplaced items on the line, the same way on every shift.
- Drones, mapping & sensor rigs: Calibrate cameras and LiDAR in the field without boards, and keep multi-sensor maps aligned.

Why it's different:
- Production experience: perception deployed on autonomous mobile robots and driver-assistance platforms at Virya Autonomous Technologies.
- Built for the field, not the benchmark: changing light, drifting sensors, dropped frames and accuracy lost on small chips are found and fixed before customers see them.
- Geometry done right: cameras and LiDAR that agree with each other, calibrated without boards, so fused 3D perception can be trusted.
- Real time on the edge: models fitted to small accelerators with the speed–accuracy trade-off measured, not guessed.

In Azad's words: I work on perception for autonomous mobile robots and driver assistance at Virya Autonomous Technologies: detection, segmentation, pose, tracking, depth and LiDAR, running on edge hardware in customer deployments. The hard part is never the demo. It's the field: light that changes, sensors that drift, a model that loses accuracy when it's squeezed onto a chip, a stream that drops frames. That's what I help robotics, automotive and physical-AI teams with: perception that ships, and keeps working once it has.

Example walkthrough (illustrative sample, not a client case): input "Front, rear and both mirror cameras streaming; a motorbike closing fast in the right lane." → Stitch: One 360° top-down view around the car, refreshed every frame; Detect: Motorbike, right lane, behind the right mirror (0.91); Locate: Placed on the ground: inside the right blind-spot zone, 1.4 m from the car; Warn: Right mirror warning on; clears as soon as the bike has passed → Result: Blind-spot alert raised in real time on the vehicle's own computer. Illustrative walkthrough.

### Document Intelligence

Hook: When your team reads the same PDF for the fifth time.

Problem: Contracts, invoices and reports hold critical data that people still copy out by hand. Extraction is slow, inconsistent and hard to audit.

Capabilities:
- Ask questions across one or many documents
- Extract fields into structured JSON
- Summarise long documents
- Compare documents and flag inconsistencies

Typical customers: Legal-tech, Finance, Insurance, HR, Enterprise SaaS

How it's used:
- Legal: Find clauses, compare contract versions and see exactly what changed.
- Accounts payable: Turn invoices into checked data and match them to purchase orders.
- Real estate: Pull rent, deposits, renewal dates and notice periods out of leases.
- HR & compliance: Answer policy questions with the paragraph that says so.

Why it's different:
- Answers with receipts: every answer shows the exact passage it came from.
- Says “the document doesn't say” instead of guessing.
- Catches mistakes before you pay: totals, tax and order mismatches are checked on every invoice.

In Azad's words: A document system is only useful if you can check its work. So everything I build answers with receipts: the page, the passage, the exact span it read. If the evidence isn't in the document, it says so instead of guessing. And before anything goes live, it's tested against your real documents, not a tidy sample.

Example walkthrough (illustrative sample, not a client case): input "What's the termination notice period, and is there an auto-renewal?" → Find: Relevant clauses: §11.2 Termination (p.2), §3.1 Term & Renewal (p.1); Read: §11.2: “…either party upon sixty (60) days’ written notice…”; Read: §3.1: “…renews automatically for successive 12-month terms…”; Verify: Both claims grounded in cited text · no conflicting clauses found → Answer: 60 days’ written notice (§11.2, p.2). Yes — it auto-renews for 12-month terms unless cancelled (§3.1, p.1).

### AI Data Analytics

Hook: When the dashboard has 40 charts and no answers.

Problem: Business data is locked behind SQL and analysts; decisions wait on reports.

Capabilities:
- Ask questions about business data
- Generate reports and visualisations
- Forecast sales and demand
- Spot unusual patterns
- Predict customer churn

Typical customers: SaaS, Retail, Finance, Operations

How it's used:
- Retail & distribution: Sales by region, top customers and slow-moving stock, on demand.
- Finance: Receivables, overdue amounts and cash collected this quarter, without a report request.
- Leadership: What changed this week and why, without waiting on an analyst.
- Operations: Stock-outs and delays spotted before customers notice.

Why it's different:
- Ask in plain English and get a number you can check, with a short note on what was counted.
- Uses your business's own definitions, so “revenue” means the same thing every time.
- Read-only: asking a question can never change your data.

In Azad's words: Asking your data a question in plain English is easy to demo and hard to get right. The trick is showing your work: the assumptions and the numbers behind every chart, without anyone being able to change your data. “Revenue” means the same thing every time, and forecasts and alerts appear only where they'll change a decision.

Example walkthrough (illustrative sample, not a client case): input "Which region's sales dropped the most last month, and why?" → Understand: Net sales · October vs September · by region; Query: SELECT region, SUM(net) … WHERE month IN (Sep, Oct) GROUP BY region; Find: West: −18% (largest drop) · driven by 2 stores, both stock-outs in week 3; Chart: Bar chart by region + store-level drill-down → Answer: West fell 18% MoM, almost entirely from two stores that ran out of the top SKU in week 3 (synthetic data).

### AI Evaluation & Monitoring

Hook: When “it seemed fine in the demo” isn't a metric.

Problem: Teams ship LLM features without knowing how often they're wrong, how fast they are, or what they cost.

Capabilities:
- Compare LLMs and prompts on fixed datasets
- Evaluate RAG answer accuracy
- Detect hallucinations and wrong answers
- Track latency, tokens and cost
- Monitor quality over time

Typical customers: AI startups shipping LLM products

How it's used:
- Any team shipping AI: Know whether a change made things better or worse before customers notice.
- Regulated industries: Evidence of accuracy and limits for audits and reviews.
- Product teams: Quality, speed and cost tracked over time on one page.
- Vision systems: Know how much accuracy a faster, smaller model really costs.

Why it's different:
- Fixed test sets with known answers, re-run before every change.
- Measures what the business cares about: accuracy, honesty, speed and cost.
- Publishes the bad news too: what fails, and where.

In Azad's words: This is the part of AI work I enjoy most, and the part most teams skip. Before swapping models or rewriting prompts, I build a fixed test set from your real traffic, define what “correct” means, and measure. Then every change is a number, not a vibe. I've done this rigorously in my own research too — benchmarking quantised models under degraded inputs — and the habit transfers directly to LLM products.

Example walkthrough (illustrative sample, not a client case): input "Support bot: current prompt vs. new prompt + reranker, on 200 golden questions." → Run: 200 questions × 2 configurations · fixed seed; Score: Correct: 78% → 88% · Grounded: 81% → 94%; Cost: p95 latency: 2.1s → 2.6s · cost per 1k answers: +12%; Inspect: Remaining failures: 14 refund-policy questions with outdated docs → Recommendation: Ship the new config; fix the refund docs first — that alone covers half the remaining failures (illustrative numbers).

### DocDesk: Answers, Fields and Checks from Business Documents — /work/docdesk

Client/context: Self-initiated · product demo · Year: 2026 · Tags: AI Automation, Document Intelligence, Full-stack

A document desk for Indian businesses: ask a contract a question and see the exact clause highlighted, turn invoices into checked data, match invoices to purchase orders, and redline contract versions.

Problem: Finance, legal and HR teams still read the same PDFs line by line: hunting for a notice period, retyping invoice totals, checking each line against the purchase order. It is slow, mistakes slip through, and nobody can show where a number came from.

Azad's contribution: Designed and built the whole product: the document library and reader, question answering that cites the page, field extraction with human approval and export, invoice and contract checks, order-to-invoice matching, version redlines, a review queue, and the quality report that grades it.

Results:
- Questions answered correctly: 100%
- Answers citing the right clause: 100%
- Fields extracted correctly: 90/90
- Typical answer time: 0.9 s

Lessons:
